clue.text: Essentially, fat insects pumped with lead shot, then pared off

indicators.note: something pumped with a substance is filled up by it, so the insects take letters inside

parts.note: midges are tiny flying insects

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked, telling us to jumble the letters of lead
off as in gone bad, telling us to scramble the letters of pared

explanation.surface: A grim recipe: fatty insects stuffed with lead pellets, then trimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead shot' reads as ammunition, but 'shot' and 'off' are both scramble signals, making DLEA and PREAD; 'then' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The paunch people tend to gain in their forties and fifties is, at heart, just fat, so the definition is a loose description.

clue.text: Torch, innocent thing in iron and gold

indicators.note: the lamb sits in the middle of the iron symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a lamb is the stock image of innocence
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Describes a torch as some innocent object set in iron and gold, like an ornate lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaming torch, especially one carried in processions, is the French-derived word for a burning brand.

clue.text: Certain limit

definitions.meaning: sure to happen, as in 'destined to win'

explanation.surface: A terse phrase about a definite boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as an adjective meaning sure or destined and as a noun meaning a limit, as in 'out of bounds'.

clue.text: Giant captured by boy, well I never!

indicators.note: the giant is held inside the boy, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a son is a boy
a troll is a giant of Scandinavian folklore

explanation.surface: An astonished cry when a little lad manages to catch a giant.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an informal British exclamation of surprise or disbelief, much like 'well I never' or 'blimey'.

clue.text: Briefly witty as some comic, I'm on guard being sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
some of the following words means only part of their letters is used

explanation.surface: A comedian on watch, ironic and quick-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes CIMONG from 'comic, I'm on guard', and 'being sent up' turns those letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes pithy, aphoristic expression: brief sayings packed with wisdom or wit.

clue.text: Enjoy a furore very much

parts.note: to enjoy something is to like it
to kick up a stink is to cause a fuss or furore

explanation.surface: Someone who relishes causing a big fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British idiom for doing something intensely or very hard, as in 'working like mad'.

clue.text: Las Vegas establishment equally popular, business raking it in

indicators.note: the business takes in the other letters, as a firm rakes in money

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
as, as in 'as tall as', expresses equality
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A Vegas venue that is popular and a business raking in the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas is famous for its gambling halls, so a gaming house is an obvious example of an establishment there.

clue.text: Noted communication error mine, alert leader in government when trebly confused

parts.note: a sin is a moral error

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the leader, or first letter, of government is G, and trebly means taking it three times

explanation.surface: A garbled message warning that a mine is in error, with a government alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' mixes the three Gs with MINE ALERT; 'when' is only a link. 'Noted' is the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A message delivered in song is literally a communication set to musical notes, hence 'noted'.

clue.text: Dirty dog's ending in no little trouble

indicators.note: the dog's last letter goes in among the jumbled letters
to trouble is to disturb, so these letters are disturbed into a new order
the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A grubby dog getting into a big scrape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' scrambles NO LITTLE into ILLOTTEN, and the G ending 'dog' goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty money is acquired dishonestly, which is the sense of the answer: gained by improper means.

clue.text: China in Japan, damage between the two

indicators.note: the damage sits between the two letters

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals, split here into its two ones
to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: Fine porcelain in Japan, damaged by two people.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of Japanese porcelain, named after the port it was shipped from, so it is china made in Japan.

clue.text: Saving a little time, don't stay to see opera singer

indicators.note: saving as in keeping, so the time is held within the other letters

parts.note: 'do go' is the opposite of staying
min is short for minute

explanation.surface: Telling someone not to linger if they want to catch a famous tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Placido Domingo is a celebrated Spanish tenor, one of the Three Tenors.

clue.text: Union supporter on course to return in Chinese dynasty

indicators.note: the turned letters go inside the dynasty

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: on a golf course, a tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A trade union backer coming back into a Chinese dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns TEE, a palindrome, so it reads the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A coming together of people or things, as in a junction of roads or a gathering, is a union.

clue.text: Runner caught someone at the top

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon; rivers run
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A sprinter caught by a senior figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete but is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for executive, a senior manager near the top of a company.

clue.text: Straggly branch OK with tall, hollow bush

indicators.note: straggly means untidy and spread out, telling us to rearrange the letters
a hollow word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A gardener's description of a shrub with a messy branch and a tall hollow trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a thorny shrub, the sloe, common in British hedges, so it is a kind of bush.

clue.text: Spooner's poem to Chelsea that may go to one's head?

definitions.text: that may go to one's head?

indicators.note: Spooner, famed for swapping word beginnings, signals exchanging the initial sounds

parts.note: a Chelsea bun is a sweet currant pastry
a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem

explanation.surface: Verse in praise of a London district that might go to one's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening letters of BUN and SONNET gives the answer. 'Chelsea' looks like the London area or football club, but is the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed hat worn for shade is something placed on the head, and 'go to one's head' is an idiom twisted literally.

clue.text: Painter, way less than a month through the alcohol

indicators.note: the shortened month runs through the middle of the spirit

parts.note: gin is a spirit

indicators.note: less means minus, so the letters are taken away

parts.note: August is a month
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: An artist drinking his way through less than a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Gauguin was a French Post-Impressionist painter known for his Tahitian scenes.

clue.text: Picture lover in ecstasy during fling

indicators.note: these letters come during the throw, set inside it

parts.note: to fling is to cast or throw
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A film buff in raptures during a brief romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' suggests an affair but means a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A film enthusiast; pictures is an old word for the cinema, so a picture lover is a film buff.

clue.text: Monument, knock one up in church

indicators.note: these letters go inside the church abbreviation
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: taken as the word one
a tap is a light knock

explanation.surface: An instruction to knock a statue up in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the word one backwards to ENO. 'knock up' tempts as a phrase, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A war memorial honouring the dead buried elsewhere, like the one in Whitehall, is a monument.

clue.text: A quality detailed, and among the best, as a nation's aspiration for a better life

definitions.text: a nation's aspiration for a better life

indicators.note: detailed read as de-tailed, the last letter cut off

parts.note: merit is a good quality

indicators.note: the word and is placed among the letters of the best

parts.note: the cream is the best of anything

explanation.surface: Praising a nation's ideal of quality and excellence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed: the quality loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal that anyone in the United States can prosper through hard work is that country's hope for a better life.

clue.text: Drooling, one throwing up during chant

indicators.note: the thrower comes during the singing, inside it

parts.note: to chant is to sing
a lobber throws the ball high up

explanation.surface: A sick, slavering football fan throwing up in the middle of a terrace chant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing up' suggests vomiting, but means tossing high.
explanation.definitionFit: Dribbling saliva from the mouth is drooling, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Leg before wicket partly, one way to get out?

indicators.note: before puts the leg term ahead of the wicket term

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a bail is one of the two small crosspieces on top of the stumps, part of the wicket

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: leg before wicket, one of the ways a batsman can be out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes LBW (leg before wicket), a cricket dismissal, but the pieces are read separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect released from custody pending trial on a payment is let out of jail, so this is a way to get out.

clue.text: US property concerned with key industry, ultimately

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: American real estate tied to a vital industry, in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The American term for real estate, land and buildings, is property in the US.

clue.text: Shake hands on mammal with flippers

definitions.meaning: to confirm or close an agreement, as with a handshake
a marine animal that swims with flippers

explanation.surface: Greeting a flippered sea creature with a handshake.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to clinch a deal and a marine mammal that basks on rocks.

clue.text: See 18
Bird I adore's heading for flowering shrub

parts.note: the robin is a common bird

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's love for a garden bird making for a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The false acacia and its relatives form a genus of flowering trees and shrubs.

clue.text: Looking away when gran nude, is it surprising?

indicators.note: surprising suggests something unexpected, telling us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Averting one's eyes on finding grandma naked, which is hardly surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Averting the gaze, physically rotating to one side, is looking away.

clue.text: See 25
Leader, the best of the bunch?

definitions.meaning: the boss or most important person
read literally, the finest fruit in a hand of yellow fruit

explanation.surface: Asking whether the boss is the pick of the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for the boss or most important person, which literally pictures the prize fruit in a bunch.
